messages:
alex: Heads-up — we had 3 OOM kills on cluster-gpu-17 between 02:10-02:45 UTC. Root cause looks like batch admission letting through wide batches while KV memory was high after the kernel switch. Logs attached in GCS.

ops-bot: Alert: OOM on node cluster-gpu-17 (oom_killer invoked). Pod: runtime-prod-qa-12. Event: 2028-06-14T02:23:11Z.

mira: Can you paste the short profiler snapshot? curious if flash-attn vs legacy kernel changed peak allocs.

alex: Quick snapshot from the crash window (reduced):
```
# perf summary (sampled during spike)
model: text-onnx-v2
kernel: flash-attn-2
batch_size: 18 -> 24 (admitted)
token_budget_target: 4096
KV cache bytes pre-batch: 7.8GB
Estimated per-request KV delta: 220MB
GPU mem before: 11.2GB
GPU mem after admit: OOM (tries to alloc ~2.1GB)
```
We admitted a batch that required ~4.0GB extra for KV copies + activation tails.

devon: This matches suspicion: admission only used token_estimate -> token_budget, but we never folded per-request KV footprint into the admission budget. Proposed quick change: compute request_kv_est = max(kv_size_hint, tokens * avg_kv_per_token) and subtract from batch_slot_budget.

samir: We tried a naive per-request kv_est in April but used hard eviction which spiked P50 by ~60ms. Soft-evict was noisy. We need a different failsafe: avoid building large KV-heavy batches instead of evicting panically.

jules: Suggestion: two-tier admission with graceful fallbacks:
1) Admission pass estimates total_extra_kv = sum(req.kv_est) + join_overhead. If total_extra_kv + current_kv > kv_soft_limit -> refuse large-batch admission.
2) If refused, try compact_slotting: pack small KV-heavy reqs into dedicated small batches (N<=6) that use kernel variant 'mem-frugal' (slower but lower peak mem).
3) If still can't fit, fall back to single-request mode.

devon: Pseudocode for admission we can prototype quickly:
```python
def admit_batch(queue):
    slots = []
    kv_budget = KV_SOFT_LIMIT - current_kv_bytes()
    for req in queue.peek_n(64):
        est = max(req.kv_hint, req.tokens * KV_PER_TOKEN)
        if est > kv_budget:
            # mark for compact_slotting or single-mode
            req.mark_fallback()
            continue
        if batch_est + est > kv_budget or token_budget_exceeded():
            break
        add_to_batch(req)
    return assembled_batch
```

mira: Also note kernel selection: flash-attn-2 uses additional workspace allocations for certain seq_len shapes (we saw ~200–400MB extra vs kernel-x). So admission should also query kernel_workspace_est(seq_profile) per candidate batch shape and add to budget.

eli: I'll own a canary PR: implement KV-aware admission + kernel workspace estimator, plus a flag to enable compact_slotting. Plan: rollout to canary pool (3 nodes) then 5% production.

alex: For the canary, add metrics: admitted_batches_total, kv_rejected_batches, compact_slots_created, fallback_single_count, avg_batch_peak_mem. Also add a trace tag with chosen kernel variant.

mira: One more experiment: simulate admission with historical traces from 2028-05 to 2028-06 to tune KV_PER_TOKEN and KV_SOFT_LIMIT. We should avoid overly conservative defaults — measure P50 latency delta under compact_slotting.

samir: Heads-up: if compact_slotting uses 'mem-frugal' kernel, we need to ensure it doesn't regress 95p by >10ms for latency-SLO customers. If it does, prefer single-request fallback.

eli: Timeline: PR today -> unit tests + perf sim tomorrow -> canary Thursday. Will post link to PR here.

alex: Great. If everyone agrees, proceed. Thanks. :thumbsup:
